initiative: Permanent marketing reset: brand-led, ~90% direct or unpaid traffic
claimed_effect: Marketing stays a far smaller share of revenue than 2019 forever
claim_source: Chesky, 4Q20 call: 'We don't intend to ever again spend the amount of money as a percentage of revenue on marketing... as we did in 2019'; 10-K S&M split table
evidence_of_realisation: Brand and performance marketing was 23.7% of revenue in 2019 ($1,140M / $4,805M) and has been 12.1-13.1% every year 2021-2025 (13.0% in 2025). But 1H26 it is 17.4% of revenue against 15.4% in 1H25, $1,091M vs $824M, +32% y/y.
quantified_effect: Worth about 11 points of margin against the 2019 cost structure; but brand and performance marketing is +2.0 points of revenue higher in 1H26 than in 1H25, so the reset is being spent back.

claimed_effect: Fixed-cost base reset; grow revenue without growing headcount
claim_source: FY2020 10-K; Stephenson, 4Q22 call
evidence_of_realisation: May 2020 workforce reduction (~1,900 roles) and the move to a functional organisation. Headcount at end-2022 (6,811) was still about 5% below 2019 on 75% more revenue (Stephenson, 4Q22 call).
quantified_effect: The single largest lever in the record and it predates the window: it is the base on which every later percentage sits, not a repeatable one.

claimed_effect: Headcount grows slower than revenue
claim_source: 10-K Item 1 Human Capital counts; 4Q25 call ('headcount growth lower than 2025' for 2026)
evidence_of_realisation: Revenue per employee $977k (2021) -> $1,521k (2024) -> $1,493k (2025), the first decline. Headcount 6,811 (2022) -> 7,300 -> 8,200, +12% in 2025. 1H26 10-Q attributes the increase in every people line (ops +$41M, product dev +$132M, S&M payroll, G&A +$38M) to higher average headcount.
quantified_effect: Productivity gain stalled: revenue per employee -1.8% in 2025 after +56% 2021-24.

initiative: Payments: in-house platform, processor mix, chargeback controls
claimed_effect: Lower merchant fees and chargebacks per dollar of GBV
claim_source: FY2021 10-K MD&A (merchant fees 3% of GBV in 2020, 2% in 2021); Chesky on the payments platform
evidence_of_realisation: Merchant fees plus chargebacks as a percent of GBV: 2.51% (2020), 1.80% (2021), then 1.89% / 1.87% / 1.84% / 1.82%. Levels after 2021 are derived from the MD&A deltas, not disclosed. Cost of revenue per $100 of GBV was $2.29 in 2Q22 and $2.33 in 2Q26.
quantified_effect: -71 bps of GBV taken out in 2021 (~1.5 points of margin); flat +-4 bps since. Not a forward lever.

claimed_effect: Lower cost of revenue
claim_source: 2Q23 letter cost-of-revenue commentary; Mertz, 2Q24 call ('will not recur')
evidence_of_realisation: 2Q23 cost of revenue carried a payment-processor incentive; Mertz on the 2Q24 call flagged 'the one-time benefit that we had in payment processing a year ago that will not recur this year'. Cost of revenue per $100 GBV was $2.26 in 2Q23 vs $2.39 in 2Q24 and $2.29 in 2Q22.
quantified_effect: One quarter, not a run-rate lever. Never sized by the company.

claimed_effect: Variable, lower-cost support capacity
evidence_of_realisation: Third-party (contingent) community-support workers: 11,000 in 2022-2024, 13,000 in 2025 (10-K Item 1). Operations and support cash cost per night $2.32 (2Q22) -> $2.30 (2Q25) -> $2.18 (2Q26).
quantified_effect: Ops and support cash per night -6% over four years while ADR rose; ~0.8 points of margin 2022-2025 (abnb_margin_bridge.csv).

claimed_effect: Support cost per booking falls, keeps falling as languages and voice roll out
claim_source: 3Q25 letter (US, -15% need for a human agent); 4Q25 letter (~1/3 resolved); 1Q26 letter (>40%); 2Q26 letter (~45%, 50+ languages, cost per booking -16%); 2Q26 10-Q (third-party -$17M)
evidence_of_realisation: Disclosed: AI assistant resolves ~1/3 of issues without an agent (4Q25 letter), over 40% (1Q26 letter), nearly 45% in 50+ languages (2Q26 letter). Customer-support cost per booking -10% y/y (1Q26 call) and -16% y/y (2Q26 letter and call). 2Q26 10-Q: third-party service-provider costs -$17M in the quarter and -$15M in 1H26 'due to lower agent contact volume resulting from increased use of artificial intelligence'. Independently: ops and support cash per night $2.13 (1H25) -> $2.05 (1H26), -3.8%.
quantified_effect: Ops and support cash per night -3.8% y/y in 1H26 = about +0.39 points of margin. Partly offset inside the same line by payroll +$41M, customer relations +$14M and insurance +$9M, so the reported line still grew 8%.

initiative: AI engineering productivity (60% of code AI-authored)
claimed_effect: More output per engineer; implied product-dev leverage
claim_source: 1Q26 call (60% of code); 2Q26 call (80% more features shipped, concept-to-launch -60%)
evidence_of_realisation: Claims: 60% of code AI-authored (1Q26 call), 80% more features shipped y/y and concept-to-launch time down as much as 60% (2Q26 call). Product development cash cost 1H25 $669M -> 1H26 $749M, +12%; the 10-Q says the whole increase is payroll on higher average headcount. Cash product development was 10.9% of revenue in 2Q22 and 10.4% in 2Q26.
quantified_effect: Zero measurable P&L saving so far. It shows up as output (features shipped), not cost. Treat as a growth option, not a margin lever.

initiative: Cloud and hosting optimisation, reserved-instance purchases
claimed_effect: Contain hosting cost growth below volume growth
claim_source: 10-K MD&A cost-of-revenue deltas; 2Q26 10-Q (server costs +$15M, reserved-instance amortisation); 10-K purchase obligations
evidence_of_realisation: 10-K MD&A gives only the increase in cloud / data-hosting cost: +$25M, +$31M, +$26M, +$27M. 1H26 10-Q: server costs +$15M 'driven by higher amortization related to reserved instance purchases and increased infrastructure spend'. Non-cancelable purchase obligations at year end: $1,068M (2022), $934M, $719M, $1,749M. The data-hosting commitment went from 'at least $672 million... through 2027' (FY2024 10-K) to 'at least $1.7 billion... through 2031' (FY2025 10-K).
quantified_effect: No disclosed saving, and the direction has reversed: committed compute is 2.4x higher at end-2025 than end-2024 and now runs to 2031. Reserved instances convert a variable cost into a fixed one. This is where the AI build is visible before it reaches the P&L.

initiative: G&A discipline and lapping of non-income tax reserves
claimed_effect: G&A grows near zero while revenue compounds
claim_source: 10-K / 10-Q MD&A G&A commentary; FY2024 non-income taxes -$656M; 1H26 -$38M
evidence_of_realisation: G&A cash cost 8.9% of revenue in 2Q22 -> 6.2% in 2Q26. 1H26 10-Q: G&A up $4M, or 1%, with payroll +$38M offset by non-income taxes -$38M. FY2024 carried a -$656M non-income-tax swing as the 2023 Italy withholding settlement reversed.
quantified_effect: The cleanest line in the P&L: roughly 2.7 points of revenue taken out since 2022, but ~1 point of it is lapping tax reserves, not operating discipline.

claimed_effect: Cheaper supply growth and better listing quality without Airbnb-employed support
claim_source: 3Q24 and 4Q24 letters; 2Q25 letter (100k listings, 10M nights)
evidence_of_realisation: Co-Host Network launched Oct 2024 (3Q24 letter). Almost 100,000 listings four months in (4Q24 letter); over 100,000 listings and 10 million cumulative nights by 2Q25. Listings on the network 'earn approximately twice as much as Airbnb listings in comparable countries' (4Q24 letter).
quantified_effect: A supply-acquisition and quality program, not a cost program. No cost effect has ever been disclosed and none is visible in field operations and policy.
verdict: Realised as a program, no cost effect disclosed

cost_line: S&M field operations and policy; product development
claimed_effect: Upfront investment, 'optimize the margins over time'
claim_source: 4Q24 letter and call; Mertz, 2Q25 call ('about $200M... field operations, go-to-market and supply acquisition'); FY2025 10-K S&M split
evidence_of_realisation: Guided $200-250M in 2025 to launch and scale Services and Experiences (4Q24 letter and call), refined to about $200M on the 2Q25 call. Field operations and policy went from $693M (2024) to $993M (2025), +43%, i.e. 6.2% -> 8.1% of revenue; S&M third-party service-provider costs rose $102M in 2025 for 'product launch and supply acquisition'. In 1H26 field ops is $535M vs $430M, +24%, decelerating from +43%.
quantified_effect: The $200-250M was spent and then some (field ops alone +$300M): about 1.9 points of revenue. Return not evidenced: no contribution margin, revenue or booking figure for Services or Experiences has ever been given.

initiative: Host fee simplification: single 15.5% fee ('Project Hawaii')
claimed_effect: Simpler pricing, no take-rate headwind
claim_source: 4Q25 print coverage; 2026 guide of a flat take rate
evidence_of_realisation: Implied take rate (revenue / GBV): 12.96% (2Q24), 13.17% (2Q25), 13.26% (2Q26). 'Project Hawaii', a single 15.5% host-paid fee replacing the split fee for property-manager listings, started rolling out in 4Q25 (revealed 12 Feb 2026). Management guides the 2026 take rate flat, held down by customer incentives on new businesses.
quantified_effect: Not yet visible. FY2025 take rate fell 16 bps (-0.8 points of margin, abnb_margin_bridge.csv). +10 bps is worth about +0.48 points of margin.

claimed_effect: Higher conversion and booking volume
claim_source: 3Q25 and 4Q25 letters; FCF bridge unearned fees
evidence_of_realisation: Reserve Now, Pay Later launched in the US in 3Q25 with ~70% adoption among eligible bookings; merchandised from 4Q25. Change in unearned fees: +$278M (2022), +$245M, +$189M, +$127M, and negative in 2Q26.
quantified_effect: Revenue-positive, cash-flow-negative: the float added 3.3 points of revenue to cash flow in 2022 and about nothing now. Roughly 2.8 points of the FCF-margin decline since 2023.

claimed_effect: Smoother reported revenue and margin
claim_source: Every 2025-2026 guide: 'after factoring in our hedging program'
evidence_of_realisation: FX hedging of forecast revenue began in 2025; every 2026 guide quotes the FX effect 'after factoring in our hedging program' (2Q26 letter: about a 3-point FX tailwind to revenue growth).
quantified_effect: Dampens, does not remove: ~0.26 points of margin per 1% dollar move unhedged (margin-drivers note section 14), less and lagged after hedges.

initiative: Investment-grade debt: $2.5B senior notes, converts repaid
claimed_effect: Cheaper permanent capital, no convert dilution
claim_source: 8-K Mar 2026; 2Q26 10-Q debt note and income statement
evidence_of_realisation: Inaugural investment-grade ratings (S&P A-, Moody's Baa1) 12-19 Mar 2026; $2.5B senior notes at 4.40-5.25%; $2.0B used to repay the 2026 converts. 2Q26 10-Q: interest expense $37M in the quarter and $58M in 1H26, against $6M and $11M a year earlier; interest income $183M vs $190M.
quantified_effect: Removes the convert dilution overhang and costs about $124M a year of interest, roughly 0.9% of revenue, below the EBITDA line. Net interest 1H26 $280M vs $352M in 1H25.

claimed_effect: Offset SBC dilution and shrink the count
claim_source: abnb_capital_return_quarterly.csv from the letters
evidence_of_realisation: Buybacks $2,139M in 1H26 against SBC of $897M; diluted share count 597M, -4.6% y/y, after -3.5% in 4Q25.
quantified_effect: SBC is 13.5% of revenue in 2Q26. Buybacks are running ahead of SBC (share count -4.6% y/y), so the dilution offset is now a real return, not just a mop-up.

initiative: Trust, safety and insurance cost containment
claimed_effect: Insurance grows slower than nights
claim_source: 10-K MD&A operations-and-support insurance deltas; 2Q26 10-Q +$9M
evidence_of_realisation: Increase in insurance cost inside operations and support: +$42M (2021), +$30M, +$16M, +$25M, +$14M; +$9M in 1H26 (2Q26 10-Q, host liability premiums). AirCover / Host Liability Insurance scales with nights.
quantified_effect: Growth in the insurance add has fallen from $42M a year to about $18M a year while nights roughly doubled: contained, but it is a cost that only goes up.

claimed_effect: Paid channels stay a small, high-ROI top-up
claim_source: 3Q24 call ('really great efficiencies'); 1Q25 call ('relative efficiencies by channel, by market')
evidence_of_realisation: Management line, repeated on five calls: '90% of our traffic remains direct or unpaid'. Performance marketing described as running at 'really great efficiencies' (3Q24 call). 1H26 10-Q: marketing spend +$258M 'driven by higher paid growth marketing initiatives in emerging markets and partnerships'.
quantified_effect: Reversed in 2026: brand and performance marketing $824M (1H25) -> $1,091M (1H26), +32%, against revenue +17%. The 90%-direct claim and a 30%+ paid-marketing ramp cannot both be efficiency.

initiative: Redeploy fixed core-market brand budget into expansion markets
claimed_effect: Core-market leverage funds expansion at no net margin cost
claim_source: Mertz, 4Q24 call; 1H26 10-Q ('emerging markets and partnerships')
evidence_of_realisation: Mertz, 4Q24 call: 'Brand marketing is effectively a fixed amount of spend for each market... the marketing budget is allowed to expand and be more heavily dedicated to expansion markets.' 1H26 10-Q names 'emerging markets and partnerships' as the driver of the marketing increase.
quantified_effect: A redeployment policy, not a saving. It means core-market leverage is real but is being spent, which is exactly why the margin guide is a floor.
verdict: Realised as a policy; it is why margin does not expand

claimed_effect: First: no P&L effect. Then: a 'material increase' inside the guide
claim_source: Chesky, 4Q25 call vs Mertz, 2Q26 call; CTO hire Jan 2026
evidence_of_realisation: Chesky, 4Q25 call: 'Our investment in AI will not affect the P&L. I don't think you'll see it in the P&L.' Mertz, 2Q26 call: 'the updated guidance that we've provided obviously does assume a material increase in terms of the AI spend over the course of the year.' New CTO (Ahmad Al-Dahle, ex-Meta Llama) hired Jan 2026.
quantified_effect: Contradiction on the record. The 2026 guide contains an unquantified AI cost increase; it is the main reason to treat the 35.5% floor as a floor and not a base.

initiative: Hotels, enterprise and global-markets organisation build-out
claimed_effect: Hotel supply at portfolio scale
claim_source: 8-Ks and press: Stein (Jan), Fuldner (Mar), D'Amico (Jun), Rijvers (Sep); May 2026 Summer Release; Lark Hotels (Aug 2026)
evidence_of_realisation: Hotels org built out through 2026: VP Hotels (Andrea D'Amico, ex-Booking) Jun 2026, Chief Business Officer (Pepijn Rijvers, ex-Booking) Sep 2026, Global Head of Operations (Gus Fuldner, ex-Uber, owns safety, support, payments, insurance) Mar 2026, hotels live in 20 cities (May 2026 release), Lark Hotels partnership Aug 2026.
quantified_effect: Cost now, revenue later. Lands in field operations and policy and in operations and support payroll. No disclosed budget.
verdict: In progress, cost only so far
